 Advertisement From El Dorado Hills to the World Series: Robert Gasser’s high school coach reflects on pitcher's growth
 Robert Gasser, a Milwaukee Brewers pitcher and Oak Ridge High School alumnus, is making his hometown proud during the World Series
 Advertisement Updated: 6:32 PM PDT Oct 27, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Lee Anne Denyer Reporter From El Dorado Hills to the World Series: Robert Gasser’s high school coach reflects on pitcher's growth
 Robert Gasser, a Milwaukee Brewers pitcher and Oak Ridge High School alumnus, is making his hometown proud during the World Series
 Updated: 6:32 PM PDT Oct 27, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Lee Anne Denyer Reporter EL DORADO HILLS, Calif. — Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Robert Gasser, an El Dorado Hills native and former Oak Ridge High School standout, is making his hometown proud with an impressive World Series performance. 
 The Brewers were up three games to none against the Tampa Bay Rays Tuesday, with a chance to win their first World Series title in Game 4. 
 Advertisement “He just keeps getting better and better,” said Todd Melton, Gasser’s former high school baseball coach. "He's surrounded by great teammates, and I think he's just growing. We're watching him grow right before our eyes."
 Brewers beat Dodgers 6-2 to take 3-0 NLCS lead Melton remembered the younger ballplayer. Gasser, a left-handed pitcher, played on a strong Oak Ridge team and brought a more “rambunctious” energy than crowds now see on the mound, he said.
 "We had to tell him, like, you could be really good, so what are you going to do about it?" he said. "The next thing you know, Robert is one of the hardest workers in the weight room, became one of the strongest players we had. And every step of the way, Robert just kept succeeding and getting better and better and makes it to the Major Leagues."
 Gasser, now 27, was drafted by the San Diego Padres in 2021 before being traded to the Brewers in 2022.
 “It takes a community, a village to raise a baseball player," Melton said. "You dream big. Next thing you know, you’re pitching in the World Series.”
